title: The Language of Principles
text:
Abstract nouns such as justice, autonomy, and integrity occupy a central place in philosophical debate. They denote concepts that cannot be observed directly, yet they shape how societies organize their laws and institutions. Scholars often disagree about the precise boundaries of such terms, which is why definitions matter so much. A vague definition can undermine an entire argument.

Consider the word 'autonomy', which may refer to personal independence or to the self-governance of an institution. Readers must infer the intended sense from context, a task that demands considerable attention. Careful writers therefore anchor these nouns in concrete cases. In doing so, they transform abstract reasoning into claims that others can evaluate.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, why does the definition of abstract terms matter?
options: Because a vague definition can undermine an entire argument.
Because scholars never agree on any term.
Because laws are written only in Latin.
Because abstract nouns can be observed directly.

questions.text: What does the second paragraph say careful writers do with abstract nouns?
options: They avoid using them in any form.
They anchor these nouns in concrete cases.
They use them only in titles.

questions.text: What can be inferred about the word 'autonomy' from the second paragraph?
options: Its meaning is always fixed in every text.
Its meaning can change depending on the context.
It can only refer to physical objects.
It is never used in institutions.

questions.text: Why might readers find it difficult to evaluate an argument built only on abstract nouns?
options: Without concrete cases, the claims are hard to test against evidence.

vocabulary.definition: the ability to govern oneself or to act independently
to weaken something gradually or secretly
to fix something firmly on a stable base

paragraph_translations: Sustantivos abstractos como justicia, autonomía e integridad ocupan un lugar central en el debate filosófico. Denotan conceptos que no pueden observarse directamente, pero determinan cómo las sociedades organizan sus leyes e instituciones. Los especialistas suelen discrepar sobre los límites precisos de estos términos, por eso las definiciones importan tanto. Una definición vaga puede socavar todo un argumento.

Consideremos la palabra 'autonomía', que puede referirse a la independencia personal o a la autogestión de una institución. Los lectores deben inferir el sentido pretendido a partir del contexto, una tarea que exige bastante atención. Por eso, los escritores cuidadosos anclan estos sustantivos en casos concretos. Al hacerlo, convierten el razonamiento abstracto en afirmaciones que otros pueden evaluar.
